chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Shyness (Al-Hiyā), chastity/modesty (Al-'Afāf), and tongue-tiedness (Al-'Iyy), meaning the modesty of the tongue, not the modesty of the heart, is from faith (Al-Īmān).'

key_terms.الْحَيَاءُ: Shyness or bashfulness, a virtue in Islamic ethics
key_terms.الْعَفَافُ: Chastity or self-restraint, often referring to sexual morality or general modesty
key_terms.الْعِيُّ: Tongue-tiedness or modesty in speech; here specified as restraint of the tongue

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the relationship between shyness, modesty of the tongue, and faith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies shyness (*hiya*), chastity (*'iffa*), and tongue-restraint (*'iyy al-lisan*) as intrinsic branches of faith (*min al-iman*). The distinction that 'modesty' applies to the tongue rather than the heart underscores the Shia emphasis on verbal discipline as a visible manifestation of inner belief. This triad reflects the holistic nature of *Iman* in Shia theology, where internal virtue is validated through external conduct.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Sayqal who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The Hiyā, and the chastity, and the tiredness, meaning the tiredness of the tongue not tiredness of the heart, is from the Emān’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from al-Hassan al-Sayqal from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Bashfulness, chastity, tiredness of tongue (to shun speaking useless things), not tiredness of the heart, are from belief.’”
